Modified by Faithful Ferret.

The files in this folder are test data for the AliasVault import. They are made up: every
name, address, user name, password, one-time password seed, card number and note in them is
invented, and none belongs to a real account. A JSON file and a ZIP file cannot carry a header
of their own, and a CSV file should not, so this notice covers all of them.

Their shapes (the columns of the CSV file, the manifest of an .avux file with its field keys,
custom field definitions, one-time password entries, passkeys and attachments, and the one
JSON header that says a file is the encrypted .avex) follow the AliasVault export code and
its test files:

  synthetic.csv, old-mobile.csv
      core/client/src/transfer/export/AliasVaultCsvExportService.ts and
      core/client/src/transfer/import/importers/aliasvault/__tests__/aliasvault_mobile_app_export.csv
  synthetic-manifest.json, synthetic.avux
      core/client/src/transfer/export/AvuxManifest.ts and
      core/client/src/transfer/import/importers/aliasvault/__tests__/aliasvault.avux
      (synthetic.avux holds synthetic-manifest.json as its manifest.json, a text file as an
      attachment and a one-pixel picture as a logo; web/test/unit/importAliasVault.test.mjs
      checks that the two agree)
  passkeys-manifest.json (and ../passkeys-expected.json)
      core/models/src/vault/Passkey.ts and apps/server/Databases/AliasClientDb/Passkey.cs (the
      keys are throwaway P-256 keys made for these tests, for the site rp-a.test, and
      registered nowhere; the tests pack the manifest into an .avux file)
  encrypted.avex
      core/client/src/transfer/import/importers/aliasvault/__tests__/aliasvault.avex (the
      header only; the payload is not encrypted data and opens with nothing)
